Normalize indicators to a common scale

Source: R/idx.R
idx_normalize.Rd

Puts indicators measured in different units on a common scale so they can be combined with idx_combine().

Usage

idx_normalize(data, cols, method = c("z", "minmax", "rank"))

Arguments

data

A data frame or sf object with one row per unit.

cols

<tidy-select> Numeric indicator columns. They are replaced in place.

method

One of:

  • "z": subtract the mean and divide by the standard deviation.

  • "minmax": rescale linearly from 0 (lowest) to 1 (highest).

  • "rank": percentile rank, \((r - 1) / (n - 1)\), where tied values share the lowest rank \(r\) (see dplyr::percent_rank()).

Value

data with the cols columns normalized.

Details

Missing values stay missing and are ignored when computing means, ranges, and ranks. A column with fewer than two distinct values says nothing about how units differ, so it is an error rather than a column of zeros.

Every method keeps the direction of the indicator: higher stays higher. Reverse an indicator before normalizing if lower values should count toward a higher index.

See also

idx_combine(), idx_sensitivity().

Examples

cities <- data.frame(
  city = c("a", "b", "c", "d"),
  share = c(0.2, 0.5, 0.6, 0.9),
  isolation = c(0.3, 0.4, 0.8, 0.7)
)
idx_normalize(cities, c(share, isolation), method = "minmax")
#>   city     share isolation
#> 1    a 0.0000000       0.0
#> 2    b 0.4285714       0.2
#> 3    c 0.5714286       1.0
#> 4    d 1.0000000       0.8
idx_normalize(cities, c(share, isolation), method = "rank")
#>   city     share isolation
#> 1    a 0.0000000 0.0000000
#> 2    b 0.3333333 0.3333333
#> 3    c 0.6666667 1.0000000
#> 4    d 1.0000000 0.6666667
